description: Two-seat CF-5D, silver, in 419 Squadron markings. First flew 14 February 1974, delivered to Cold Lake and later used by AETE and 419 Squadron; to 406 (Maritime Operational Training) Squadron at Shearwater as a training aid in June 2002. Kept in museum hangar 2 where training sessions may sometimes be viewed. Canadian Warplanes also lists 116832 at Cold Lake; the Shearwater provenance is the fuller one.

Recovered from an Ontario field and restored by naval aviation enthusiasts in the Toronto area, first flying again in April 1994 at CFB Shearwater as one of only four airworthy Swordfish then in the world, and donated to the museum. Civil registration C-GRCN.
Ex-Indian Navy Firefly, construction number F.6173, registered C-GRCN.
One of 39 Banshees bought from the US Navy; arrived at Shearwater in March 1957 and flew with VF 870 Squadron from Shearwater and from HMCS Bonaventure.
Built as a TBM-3E by the Eastern Aircraft Division of General Motors at Trenton, New Jersey, and coded TFD. Later an Avenger AS.3 in Canadian service.
Flown to the museum on 26 July 2012 as water bomber aircraft 23, civil registration C-FIMR.
